title: Etale local finite free models in nonnegative degrees
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space], and use its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded module derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Tensor pullback is [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and its left derived functor is computed by K-flat resolutions. Let $K\in D(\mathcal O_B)$ be perfect, meaning etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Suppose that for every scheme morphism $g:T\to B$, the cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^i(Lg^*K)$ vanish for $i<0$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Then there is a small jointly surjective family of etale maps $u_\alpha:U_\alpha\to B$ from affine schemes $U_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}A_\alpha$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and for each $\alpha$ an integer $b_\alpha\geq0$, a complex $P_\alpha^\bullet$ on $(U_\alpha)_{\mathrm{et}}$ and an isomorphism $Lu_\alpha^*K\simeq Q(P_\alpha^\bullet)$ in $D(\mathcal O_{U_\alpha})$. Here $P_\alpha^i=0$ outside $[0,b_\alpha]$, and $P_\alpha^i=\mathcal O_{U_\alpha}^{r_{\alpha,i}}$ for finite ranks $r_{\alpha,i}$; its differentials are matrices over $A_\alpha$. The symbol $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. No uniform bound on the ranks or $b_\alpha$, and no Noetherian hypothesis, is required.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: the last two paragraphs, forming Coker(M^{-1} -> M^0), proving it finite locally free, and trivializing it on affine opens.

proof.text: Choose an etale scheme atlas of $B$ and refine by affine opens using [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. On every member, apply the local perfectness condition in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] and refine again by affine opens. The etale chart calculus [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] identifies these restrictions with derived pullbacks and supplies the composition identifications. Thus we obtain affine etale charts $u:U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to B$ with $Lu^*K\simeq Q(F^\bullet)$, where $F^\bullet$ is bounded and each $F^i$ has specified split maps to and from $\mathcal O_U^{N_i}$. Open restrictions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; composition with a representable etale chart is checked on scheme base changes. The small-site convention [def-weil-size-convention] makes all these covering families set-indexed in the prescribed universe.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: reduction to an affine scheme and the final cokernel/trivialization argument; perfectness is already a hypothesis here.

proof.text: For one such affine chart, let $e_i=i_ip_i$ be the idempotent on $\mathcal O_U^{N_i}$ from the split package. A homomorphism between finite free structure sheaves is determined by its values on the standard basis, hence is a matrix over $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)=A$. Put $M^i=\operatorname{im}(e_i:A^{N_i}\to A^{N_i})$; $A^{N_i}=\operatorname{im}(e_i)\oplus\operatorname{im}(1-e_i)$. The matrices $i_{i+1}d^ip_i$ induce differentials on these summands, and their successive composites are zero by $p_ii_i=1$ and $d^{i+1}d^i=0$. The exact affine realization $a_A$ of [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] identifies the resulting complex with $F^\bullet$: both images of each idempotent are its split image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] to each of the finitely many nonzero $M^i$ and take common principal-open refinements. Finite intersections are principal opens $D(f_1\cdots f_t)$. On each refined chart all terms become finite free, and the differential remains a matrix. Henceforth write $M^\bullet$ for this bounded finite free complex and $C^\bullet=\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ for its Zariski associated complex; $a_A(M^\bullet)=\epsilon_U^*C^\bullet$ represents $Lu^*K$. The affine equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] ensures that $Q(C^\bullet)$ belongs to the Zariski derived subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology, as needed for the derived topology comparison in step 3.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: reduction to an affine scheme and the final cokernel/trivialization argument; perfectness is already a hypothesis here.

proof.text: Let $A\to D$ be any commutative algebra, and $h:\operatorname{Spec}D\to U$. The universal hypothesis, applied to $uh$, and the composition comparison of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] give $\mathcal H^j(Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*Lu^*K)=0$ for $j<0$. The derived pullback comparison of [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] identifies this object with $\epsilon_{\operatorname{Spec}D}^*Lh^*C^\bullet$. Since $C^\bullet$ is bounded and finite free, [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback] computes the latter Zariski pullback termwise. The affine pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], natural in the module and thus compatible with differentials, identifies it with $\widetilde{M^\bullet\otimes_A D}$. Consequently its etale extension is $a_D(M^\bullet\otimes_A D)$. Exactness, faithfulness, and the cohomology clause of [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] imply $H^j(M^\bullet\otimes_A D)=0$ for every $j<0$.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: reduction to an affine scheme and the final cokernel/trivialization argument; perfectness is already a hypothesis here.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $A$-module $N$ form the commutative square-zero algebra $D=A\oplus N$, with $(a,n)(a',n')=(aa',an'+a'n)$ and unit $(1,0)$. As complexes of $A$-modules, $M^\bullet\otimes_A D=M^\bullet\oplus(M^\bullet\otimes_A N)$: the differential respects the displayed summands. Kernels and images of a block-diagonal map are the corresponding direct sums. Applying degree $-1$ cohomology to the vanishing proved in step 3 therefore gives $H^{-1}(M^\bullet\otimes_A N)=0$ for every module $N$. Taking $D=A$ in step 3 also gives $H^j(M^\bullet)=0$ for all $j<0$.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: reduction to an affine scheme and the final cokernel/trivialization argument; perfectness is already a hypothesis here.

proof.text: The modules $M^i$ are free, hence flat: tensor with $A^r$ is the finite direct sum of $r$ copies of the identity and preserves exact sequences. Apply [lem-pc-module-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] with $a=0$ and the universal degree-minus-one vanishing from step 4. It proves that $Z=\operatorname{coker}(M^{-1}\to M^0)$ is flat. The displayed map is between finite free modules, so $Z$ has a finite presentation, including when one of these ranks is zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective], $Z$ is finite projective.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: reduction to an affine scheme and the final cokernel/trivialization argument; perfectness is already a hypothesis here.

proof.text: Define $E^j=0$ for $j<0$, $E^0=Z$, and $E^j=M^j$ for $j>0$, with the induced differential $Z\to M^1$. It is well defined since $d^0d^{-1}=0$. The chain map $q:M^\bullet\to E^\bullet$ is the quotient in degree zero, the identity in positive degrees and zero in negative degrees. In degree zero, $\ker(Z\to M^1)=\ker d^0/\operatorname{im}d^{-1}$, so $H^0(q)$ is an isomorphism. In positive degrees the kernels and images agree, and in negative degrees both cohomologies vanish by step 4. Thus $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Exactness of $a_A$ [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] makes $a_A(q)$ a quasi-isomorphism too. Localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives an isomorphism $Lu^*K\simeq Q(a_A(E^\bullet))$ in the derived category, not merely separate cohomology isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08JX, lemma-cohomology-perfect-complex, proof: reduction to an affine scheme and the final cokernel/trivialization argument; perfectness is already a hypothesis here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] to $Z$ and refine this chart by the resulting principal opens. Exact etale restriction and its composition comparisons [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] restrict the derived isomorphism of step 6. After choosing a basis of each localized $Z$, all terms of the resulting complex $P^\bullet$ are finite free structure modules. Its differentials are matrices over the affine coordinate ring, by their values on the standard basis. If $d$ is an upper support bound for the original bounded complex, take $b=\max(0,d)$; then $P^j=0$ outside $[0,b]$. All refinements cover their parent, so their composites remain jointly surjective and small as in step 1. The bounds and ranks are chosen separately on each chart. The construction permits the empty space, zero complex, zero ranks, and arbitrary commutative coordinate rings; no Noetherian or uniform-bound assumption was used.
